observation.visible_scene: A single white swan (tundra/whooper type) with a yellow-and-black bill floats upright on calm, pale blue-grey water, its body and neck mirrored in a clear reflection directly beneath it. Behind and above the bird is a dark muddy/grassy shoreline dotted with stones, and a few strands of floating dark twigs/debris lie on the water surface near the swan. A gentle wake and concentric ripple lines trail off to the right of the bird. The dark shape under the swan is its reflection, not a second object; the small dark specks on the water are detached debris.
visible_changes: The swan drifts slowly leftward across the frame over the excerpt (head from roughly mid-frame toward the left third), while keeping an upright neck and left-facing bill posture throughout.

Relative to the swan, the background shoreline and the floating twigs/debris shift rightward, consistent with the bird making slow forward progress through the water rather than merely bobbing in place.
The mirror reflection tracks the swan's position and posture continuously, elongating/shortening slightly as the water surface ripples.
Ripple/wake lines on the right side of the frame persist and slowly reform, indicating ongoing low-speed motion.
The swan's head/neck angle changes only marginally (a slight tilt of the bill at times); no major pose change, submersion, or action onset/offset is seen.

The framing of the bank at the top of the image changes gradually, suggesting a slight camera pan/zoom following the bird, but the swan's leftward drift relative to the debris is the dominant real motion.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the swan began or will end its glide outside this segment (the excerpt shows an ongoing drift, not a start or stop).
What lies beyond the visible shoreline and whether the bird is heading toward or away from it.
The cause of the camera's slight reframing (operator pan vs. digital crop movement) is not determinable from the clip.
uncertain_details: Exact split between camera pan/zoom and the swan's own translation: absolute frame positions move modestly, but the swan-vs-debris relative shift confirms real leftward motion.
Precise swimming speed and direction cannot be quantified; only slow leftward drift is supported.
Minor bill/neck orientation differences between frames may be natural bobbing rather than deliberate head turning.
